records.purpose: Copy the local player's current item-port snapshot into out (caller sets out->size; out->count is capacity in, ports filled out, max 128). The ports are the whole attached tree, depth first: each port, then the ports of the container attached to it, empty ports included. Read-only: per valid port, the attached item's item type id (field item_class_id, an ordinal of the game's item-type enumeration) and its session-scoped entity id (joins game.entities); generation advances on port-set change. With out->size >= sizeof(sc_inventory_snapshot) (1.1) it also sets flags (TRUNCATED: ports beyond the cap exist; LIMITED: the walk's own limits cut the tree) and total_seen; a 1.0 caller passing the 1.0 size never sees them. Values are the client's view of server state at snapshot time; nothing can be written through this ABI.

records.ownership: Provider fills caller-owned storage; a plain copy crosses. No allocation, no engine pointer transfer, nothing retained from out.
records.reentrancy: Snapshot read; the adapter reads the container's port vector in place and calls only per-port accessors, each checked against its signature row first.
records.results: OK snapshot copied, UNAVAILABLE service off, no backend bound, out null, out->size below the 1.0 snapshot size, no local player, no item-port container on the player, or the adapter's guards failed; BAD_ARG invalid self.
records.absent_capability: game.inventory.read defaults OFF (a product switch, and every inventory.* signature row must be OK); off, unbound or unready, the service publishes UNAVAILABLE. Adapter grounded on the private corpus (F-4.10.197.2878-011..-016); synthetic evidence only, not run in game.
records.cleanup: StopGameInventory withdraws the service; read-only, no engine state to restore.
limitations: Local player ports only in 1.0 (ships/mounts are follow-ups).
Per-class item names are not yet established; an item-type-id name map exists but is not exposed.

Snapshot semantics: 128 ports max; the walk covers the whole attached tree depth first (at most 8 levels below the player's container, 256 containers, 4096 ports counted); flags and total_seen say what was cut; generation is computed by comparing successive snapshots (the game has no change counter); per-frame streams are out of contract.
Nesting is not reported: ports come in walk order without a parent or depth.
No C# or Lua game.inventory routes are supported.
